title: Prove the eight-query mutable-source tariff is exactly 460 (no κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped exact finite computation with a finite certificate, in the PR1898 abstract tariff. No κ.** In the path-lowered even-subset class of [#2677](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2677) (`research/mutable-source-789q-invoice`), every eight-query word needs at least 74 readouts `R` and at least 4 source XORs `X`, and one closed walk attains both. The eight-query row of #2677's table was a lower bound (`R >= 74`, `X >= 0`, tariff `>= 452`). It is now exact:

```text
min over eight-query words of  b*Q + a*R + x*X  =  8b + 74a + 4x   for all b, a, x > 0
tariff at (b, a, x) = (38, 2, 2):  460, which is 24 above the six-query endpoint 436
witness (R = 74, X = 4):  closed prefix walk (0, 1, 3, 2, 6, 14, 30, 20, 0)
```

What was known and what is new. `R >= 74` is #2677's census. `X >= 4` is the connector consequence recorded in [#5935](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5935) (this author) with the component inequality of [#2455](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2455); a two-line proof for the path-local class is included for self-containment. New here:

- One walk attains both floors, so the Pareto frontier at `Q = 8` is the single point `(74, 4)` and the optimum is price-independent. The same holds at `Q = 6`, `(96, 8)`, and `Q = 7`, `(82, 6)`, which are existing values this package reproduces.
- Exact census spectra over every set of 5, 6 and 7 connector values. Repeated prefix values force `R >= 82`, so the exact minimum at eight queries is 74 with repeats allowed, attained only with seven distinct nonzero values. This answers Open next question 2 of #2677 and the readout half of Open next question 2 of [#2686](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2686) within the class.
- Sharp XOR floor 4 at eight queries for arbitrary restored words, from #5935's lower bound and the attaining word (Open next question 2 of [#2643](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2643)).
- Exhaustive X-floor layers at `Q = 6..10` (271,170, 604,800, 730,800, 453,600 and 113,400 walks, equal to the closed-form count) and an attained value 486 at `Q = 9` (floor 470).
- Crossovers among `Q = 6, 7, 8`: `f8 < f7` iff `b < 8a + 2x`, `f7 < f6` iff `b < 14a + 2x`, `f8 < f6` iff `b < 11a + 2x`. At `(38, 2, 2)` all fail, so the six-query endpoint stays optimal among `Q <= 8`.

## Evidence and reproduction

Python 3.12, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/eight-query-path-lowered-tariff/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eight-query-path-lowered-tariff
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/eight-query-path-lowered-tariff --check-source-history
```

All three passed locally. Timings: verifier 53.6 s, registered replay 49.7 s. Expected marker: `PASS_EIGHT_QUERY_PATH_LOWERED_TARIFF Q8=(R74,X4) tariff=460 floors_attained_Q6_Q7_Q8 Q9_in_470_486 no_new_kappa`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, then `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

The verifier imports #2677's `model.py` as a pinned live input after a SHA256 check. It checks the readout census (3,535,767 value sets, 3,097,024 covering), the path-local XOR floor exhaustively on 638,832 covering walks in `F2^2..F2^4`, every X-floor layer with its closed-form count, literal dirty-row replays of the `Q = 8` witnesses, the `Q = 7` champion, the six-query word and the `Q = 9` witness, the crossover equivalences on a price grid, and 6,000 seeded random walks against the pinned model. The exhaustive search that found the witnesses was a separate unpackaged program; every number quoted is recomputed by `verify.py`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- The exact row is for path-lowered even-subset words with #2677's tariff. Readout and spectrum claims are not checked for arbitrary XOR-interleaved restored words.
- The XOR lower bound for arbitrary restored words is #5935's with #2455's component inequality. It is cited, not re-proved here, and #2455's inequality is taken as proved for five sources.
- Nine queries are not settled (between 470 and 486). The ten-query layer is a cross-check only: it reproduces the read-only 64-readout repair and the four-XOR requirement at 62 readouts that earlier packages record. No ten-query claim is made.
- The tariff is the abstract complete-call fixture. No physical supplier, hosting or precision claim. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean or Docker run.

## Open next questions

1. What is the exact tariff at nine queries? Enumerate the `X = 6` layer (weight total 12) and compare its least readout count with 70.
2. Does the readout floor 74 hold for arbitrary XOR-interleaved restored words at eight queries? The census uses only the set of connector values, so the first step is to check that a restored word's connector values obey the same even-subset readout constraint.

## Related open work

- [#2817](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2817) (VictorLiwentao): transfer-coupled `(5,1,1)` seven-query readout obstruction. Same abstract tariff, different interface; no numbers compared.
- [#6695](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6695) (this author): toggle alphabets in the #943/#3321 connector batch. A different interface from these common-B mutable-source words. Its 72 queries and 74 additions are counts in that interface, unrelated to the readout floor 74 here; no numbers compared.
